# AgentPassport — Agent Skill

> Real-world infrastructure for AI agents: email inboxes on a domain the
> user owns, and country-anchored residential IP egress that can be pinned
> so one identity always exits from the same IP.

One CLI, one SDK, one API key. Not temp-mail — every address is bound to a
domain the user owns.

## Install

```
npm install -g @agentpassportsh/cli       # CLI
npm install @agentpassportsh/sdk          # SDK
```

## Authenticate

```
export AP_API_KEY=your_agentpassport_api_key
```

Get a key at https://agentpassport.sh.

## Capability status

- Email — receive on a domain the user owns — shipped
- Email — send from a domain the user owns — shipped
- Domains — shipped (precondition for email)
- Proxy — shipped (residential IPs by country/city, pinnable per identity)
- VPN — coming (WireGuard tunnels by region)

## Domain prerequisite (human, once per domain)

```
app domain add myagent.com
# returns 2 nameservers; user sets them at their registrar.
# 5–30 min propagation.
app domain status myagent.com --wait
```

## Email — common tasks (agent-runnable)

- Provision an inbox:
  `app email create --domain myagent.com --name support`
- Wait for the next message (msg.raw has the full RFC 5322):
  `app email watch --inbox support@myagent.com --timeout 60s --json`
- Read latest N messages (newest first):
  `app email read --inbox support@myagent.com -n 10 --json`
- Filter by substring on the raw message:
  `app email read --inbox support@myagent.com --filter "verification" --json`
- Send mail from any address on a domain the user owns (no inbox
  needs to exist for `from`; domain ownership is the only check):
  `app email send --from noreply@myagent.com --to b@y.com --subject "..." --body "..."`
  SDK: `await ap.email.send({ from, to, subject, text, html?, replyTo? })`

Every inbound message has shape:

```ts
{ id, to, receivedAt, sentAt, from, subject, text, html, code, raw }
```

`from / subject / text / html` are parsed server-side from the standard
RFC 5322 fields (spec-defined header / MIME extraction). `code` is a
best-effort server-lifted OTP — the first 4–8 digit run in subject + body,
or `null` if none. `raw` is the full original message for edge cases.

Pull a code (server already lifted it):

```
code=$(app email watch --inbox $INBOX --timeout 60s --json | head -1 | jq -r .code)
```

TypeScript:

```ts
for await (const msg of ap.email.watch({ inbox, timeoutMs: 60_000 })) {
  // msg.code is the server-lifted OTP; fall back to your own regex if the
  // sender's format is unusual.
  const code = msg.code ?? (msg.text ?? "").match(/\b\d{4,8}\b/)?.[0];
  if (code) { await externalService.verify({ email: inbox, code }); break; }
}
```

## Proxy — common tasks (agent-runnable)

- Mint a session and route the shell through it:
  `eval "$(app proxy session --country US --export)"` then `curl https://api.ipify.org`
- JSON form (host / port / username / password / expiresAt):
  `app proxy session --country US --city new-york --duration 60 --json`
- Pin an identity so every future session reuses the same IP:
  `app proxy session --country US --bind-to support@myagent.com --json`
  SDK: `await ap.proxy.session({ country: "US", bindTo: "support@myagent.com" })`
- See which keys are pinned and to which IP:
  `app proxy bindings`  ·  SDK: `await ap.proxy.bindings()`
- Release a pin (next session gets a new IP; also the only way to change
  a key's country):
  `app proxy unbind --bind-to support@myagent.com`

Without `--bind-to` every mint lands on a different IP. With it, the same
upstream session is reused, so the IP holds as long as that residential
peer stays online — best-effort, not a dedicated static IP. Sessions
themselves last up to 60 minutes (`--duration`, default 30).
